extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of North Carolina / U.S. state history (secondary or early-college level)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of chapter-level study and comprehension questions for a textbook history passage on North Carolina (1821–1846). Prompts ask students to recall facts, explain causes and effects, and situate persons, events, and institutions discussed in each chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q1: Growth in the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: What growth was noticed in the Union during the years just considered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question from Chapter XLV (The Whigs and the Democrats). Assess factual recall about national growth trends cited in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q2: Immigration to North Carolina
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of immigration to North Carolina?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Chapter XLV — prompt asks to summarize the chapter's statements on immigration patterns into NC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q3: Condition of political parties
rubrics_metrics.description: In what condition were the political parties of the country?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — asks for explanation of party organization and divisions at the time (e.g., dominance of Democratic-Republicans, lingering Federalist views).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q4: Madison administration
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of President Madison's administration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — factual recall / brief evaluation per the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q5: Lafayette's visit
rubrics_metrics.description: What distinguished Frenchman visited North Carolina in the year 1825? How was he everywhere received by the people? How did Congress treat him?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — multi-part factual recall concerning La Fayette's visit and honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q6: Cotton price rise effects
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the extraordinary rise in the price of cotton? How did it affect many people?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — asks to state the chapter's account of the cotton price spike and consequences for planters/speculators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q7: Effect of Adams election and parties
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the effect of the election of John Quincy Adams? What two political parties then existed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — identify political realignment (Adams, Jackson; Whigs vs. Democrats) and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q8: Adams' troubles and Whig principles
rubrics_metrics.description: What troubles did Mr. Adams find? What party was led by Henry Clay? What were some of the Whig principles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — recall the opposition Adams faced and summarize Whig platform items listed (Bank, protective tariff, distribution to states).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q9: Jackson and Democratic positions
rubrics_metrics.description: What did General Jackson and his party advocate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — summarize Democratic positions as given in the chapter (revenue tariff, opposition to National Bank, opposition to distribution plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q10: Results of violent assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: What results were produced by the violent assertions of these opinions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — asks for the social/political consequences (rancor, animosities, duels, breakdown of social amenities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q11: Political animosities commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of political animosities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — evaluate the chapter's moral/philosophical comment on hatred over political disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLV Q12: Slavery question and Society for African Emancipation
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the question of slavery viewed? What State refused to recognize the legality of slave property? What society was organized?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLV — combine factual recall about early abolitionist efforts and state reactions (Massachusetts, Society for African Emancipation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q1: Troublesome years overview
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of these troublesome years?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI (The Condition of the State) — general summary question about the period 1827–1836.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q2: Eastern/western divisions in NC
rubrics_metrics.description: What troubles were seen in North Carolina? What divisions had rung up between the eastern and western men of the State?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — asks to describe sectional tensions over capital location and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q3: Views on representation
rubrics_metrics.description: How did the men of the two sections view the question of representation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — explain eastern insistence on Halifax Constitution representation vs western demand for weight by population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q4: Capitol fire details
rubrics_metrics.description: What public building was burned on June 21st, 1831? What was the cause of the fire? What was lost with the building? Where was the new capitol built? Of what was it built?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — factual recall regarding the Raleigh capitol fire, loss of Canova statue, and rebuilding details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q5: Chief regret and sculptor
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the chief regret? Who was this work by?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — focuses on the lost Canova statue of Washington.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q6: Western Convention of 1823
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the Western Convention of 1823?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — summarize aims and sectional reaction described in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q7: Convention law enacted
rubrics_metrics.description: What law was enacted concerning a convention?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — recall the "Convention Bill" provisions about calling conventions and oaths limiting alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q8: Memorable Convention of 1835 changes
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the memorable convention of 1835? What changes were made in the Constitution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — list constitutional changes (abolition of borough representation and free negro suffrage, popular election of governor, biennial sessions, county representation adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q9: Vote majority and last legislature-selected governor
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the majority of the votes given to the amendments? Who was the last Governor selected by the Legislature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — factual recall about referendum margin and Governor Richard Dobbs Spaight being the last legislature-selected governor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q10: 1836 candidates and first elected governor
rubrics_metrics.description: What two candidates were before the people in 1836? Who was the first Governor elected by the people?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — identify Dudley and Spaight (or other named candidates) and the first popularly elected governor (Edward B. Dudley).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVI Q13: Northern states and slavery; Southern reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: How had the Northern States acted in regard to slavery? What checked the liberal spirit of the South concerning slavery?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVI — asks to recount Northern manumission and sale of slaves, and Southern reaction to Northern denunciations inhibiting Southern liberalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q1: Changes by 1836 and cotton/slave property
rubrics_metrics.description: What changes were noticed in North Carolina in 1836? What is said of cotton and slave property?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII (Internal Improvements—The Courts and the Bar) — factual recall on economic and social shifts (cotton cultivation; value of slave property).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q2: Dismal Swamp Canal and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: What canal had been completed? How did it benefit that section?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — recall Dismal Swamp Canal effects on trade and navigation to Norfolk and West Indies trade changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q3: Railway charters
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the railway charters?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — identify earliest railroad charters mentioned (Petersburg 1830, Portsmouth and Roanoke 1832, Wilmington Railroad) and their significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q4: Condition of railroads
rubrics_metrics.description: In what condition were railroads at this time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — describe early stage and rapid expansion as pioneer works of larger network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q5: Present means of travel (as of text)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the present means of travel?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — contrast older wagon travel with steam railroads and effects on national unity and commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q6: Baptist State Convention formation
rubrics_metrics.description: What religious convention had been formed in 1730?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — (text says 1830) recall formation of Baptist 'State Convention' and its effects on missions, periodicals, colleges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q7: Public man Willie P. Mangum
rubrics_metrics.description: What public man is now mentioned, and what is said of his abilities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — assess statement about Judge Willie P. Mangum's eloquence and election to the U.S. Senate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q8: Chief-Justice Taylor mention
rubrics_metrics.description: What mention is made of Chief-Justice Taylor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — recall praise of Chief Justice Taylor as 'Mansfield of North Carolina' and his death in 1829.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q9: Supreme Court changes and Ruffin
rubrics_metrics.description: What changes were made in the Supreme Court? What is said of Judge Thomas Ruffin?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — note succession (Toomer resigned; Ruffin joined) and Ruffin's judicial qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q10: Succession and court composition 1833
rubrics_metrics.description: Who succeeded Judge Henderson? Who composed the Supreme Court in 1833?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — factual recall: William Gaston succeeded Henderson; Court composed of Chief-Justice Thomas Ruffin, Joseph J. Daniel and William Gaston (Associates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q11: Superior Court judges names
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you name some of the Judges, of the Superior Court?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — expects listing of judges named (Thomas Settle, R. M. Saunders, John M. T. Dick, John L. Bailey, Richmond M. Pearson, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q12: The Bar at this period
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the Bar at this period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — summarize praise for Bar learning, eloquence, and named prominent lawyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVII Q13: Influence of lawyers in a community
rubrics_metrics.description: How is the influence of lawyers always felt in a community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVII — reflect the chapter's normative claim that lawyers are sentinels of liberty and influence morality next to clergy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q1: Chapter subject and education laws
rubrics_metrics.description: What is this chapter about? What laws has been enacted concert concerning education?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII (Origin of the Public Schools) — overview prompt: topic and legislation affecting education referenced in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q2: Queen's Museum incorporation refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Why had incorporation been refused to the "Queen's Museum"?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — recall that refusal stemmed from its Presbyterian affiliation while law required Church of England communicant teachers for incorporation earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q3: Schools at Charlotte and Davidson
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the schools at Charlotte and Davidson?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — recall Liberty Hall (Charlotte), Davidson College founding and private denominational support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q4: Halifax Constitution clause and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: What clause was in the first State Constitution? How had the intent of this clause been carried out?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — cite Section 41 calling for public schools/universities and discuss slow implementation prior to University at Chapel Hill and later developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q5: Views on popular education and advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: What were some of the views in regard to popular education? What men had advocated the provisions of the Constitution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — discuss opposition to taxation for education and names (Governors Johnston and Davie, Judge Murphy, Bartlett Yancey) who supported compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q6: School Fund addition in 1837
rubrics_metrics.description: What addition to the School Fund did North Carolina receive in 1837?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — recall federal distribution from sale of public lands (North Carolina's share ~ $1.5 million) and other state assets added to School Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q7: How fund was further increased
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the fund further increased?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — note swamp land sales, state bank stock, and other state property contributions to the School Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q8: Legislation affecting school matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you mention the legislation at this period affecting school matters?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — recall 1836 act creating Literary Board, 1839 act dividing counties into school districts, and 1840 free education legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q9: Denominational schools founded
rubrics_metrics.description: What denominational schools were founded about this time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — list Wake Forest (Baptists), Davidson (Presbyterians), and others mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q10: Old-field schools status
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of the "old-field schools"?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — they were superseded by academies and common schools as better institutions arose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q11: Leading male schools and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Where were the leading male schools, and what is said of the usefulness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — expects naming Bingham School, Lovejoy, Bobbitt, Caldwell Institute, Trinity College, Donaldson Academy and noting their contributions to well-informed men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLVIII Q12: Female schools and St. Mary's
rubrics_metrics.description: What female schools are mentioned? What is said of St. Mary's School? What is said of other schools?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLVIII — mentions Salem Seminary, St. Mary's (Raleigh) under Bishop Ives and other female institutions (Methodist Female College, Edgeworth) and remarks on their quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q1: Three classes of society in 1842
rubrics_metrics.description: What three classes of society existed in North Carolina in 1842?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX (Slavery and Social Development) — recall White people, slaves, and free negroes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q2: Convention of 1835 action on free negroes
rubrics_metrics.description: What action was taken by the Convention of 1835 in regard to free negroes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — recall disenfranchisement and removal of suffrage for free negroes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q3: Description of free negro class
rubrics_metrics.description: What is said of this class of our population?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — summarize negative characterizations in the chapter (unthrifty, dishonest, socially discriminated against).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q4: Southern view on slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: How did our people view the question of slavery?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — recall constitutional/property framing, view that slavery/property rights were settled by law and a private moral matter between owner and God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q5: Privileges denied the slaves and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: What privileges were denied the slaves? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — list denial of education, right to testify against whites, limited self-defense rights; chapter argues these restrictions were necessary to maintain legal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q6: Probable final result for NC
rubrics_metrics.description: What would probably have been the final result in North Carolina?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — chapter's speculation that gradual manumission and exportation might have led NC to become free given time and opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q7: Northern states' action and Southern compulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: What had the Northern States done with their slaves? How was the South compelled to act?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — recall Northern manumissions followed by sales south; South could not follow the same path and therefore resisted change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q8: Educational progress being made
rubrics_metrics.description: What educational progress was being made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — note that public education was recently adopted and beginning to show effects (children of poor receiving rudiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q9: Condition of religious matters
rubrics_metrics.description: What was the condition of religious matters?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — description of rural congregations, itinerant ministers, and limited religious observances beyond Sunday schools and meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q10: Effects from church growth
rubrics_metrics.description: What effects were seen from the growth of the churches?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — decline in balls and horse-races in eastern counties due to Methodist and Baptist influence; Presbyterians had never countenanced such amusements in the west.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter XLIX Q11: Summer congregations and camp-meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: What great congregations were found in various places during the summer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter XLIX — expect mention of protracted 'camp-meetings' serving religious devotion for many and social/courtship occasions for the young.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter L Q1: Period reached and governors (partial)
rubrics_metrics.description: What period have we now reached? Who were Governors at this time? What is said of Governor John Branch?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter L (The Mexican War) — early questions asking to situate the narrative period and recall governors and Branch's career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter L Q2: Candidates for Governor and notes on them (partial)
rubrics_metrics.description: What mention is made of the candidates for Governor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter L — recall candidates (Morehead, Saunders, etc.) and their qualities as described in the chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter L Q3: Deaths of prominent men (partial)
rubrics_metrics.description: What deaths of prominent men occurred about this period?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter L — recall deaths of Gaston, Daniel, Lewis Williams, Michael Hoke, and effects on the state political landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter L Q4: (partial)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter L — question fragment present in the chunk; full text not available in this chunk.
